parties.ourParty: The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (Company) — the customer
parties.counterparty: Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI) — the site developer/host (vendor)

plans.note: No liability heading surfaced in the outline, but the numbered body (sec-p0001 through the signature block at sec-p0072) is only partially enumerated; scan the later general/miscellaneous articles for a cap, exclusion of consequential damages and any one-sided carve-outs favouring HDI. If nothing exists, treat as missing rather than deviation.

Missing-type rule. Check the body for an HDI indemnity covering third-party IP claims arising from the developed/hosted site and from HDI's own misconduct; sec-1.4 (access to systems/materials) is the likely neighbourhood for IP-related risk allocation. Confirm any Company-side indemnity is narrow before concluding.

Presence rule — flag only if found. Nothing in the outline restricts the Company's businesses or sourcing of Deerskin Products; still sweep the body for covenants tied to competing catalogues or web channels before recording as absent.

Presence rule. A development-and-hosting deal often makes HDI the sole host; check whether sec-1.4 or the services articles say the Company must use HDI exclusively for site development/hosting. Only flag if the Company is actually locked in.

Direction rule. No pricing/most-favoured-customer language surfaced. Only a clause obliging the Company to give HDI its best terms is objectionable; an MFN running in our favour is welcome and must not be flagged.

Presence rule. sec-5.4 (each party appoints a project manager/personnel contact) is the most likely place a mutual no-hire of dedicated personnel would sit; check for duration and a general-advertising carve-out if one appears.

The defined term 'Termination Date' confirms a term/termination article exists in the unenumerated body. Locate it and test whether the Company may terminate on notice without penalty and whether HDI has a symmetric or broader mid-term exit.

Look in the same term/termination article that defines 'Termination Date' for auto-renewal, the non-renewal notice window and any renewal repricing. A missing price-uplift cap is a rationale note, not a deviation.

Boilerplate sits near the end, just before the signature block at sec-p0072. Both parties are US catalogue companies, so New York or Delaware is likely and acceptable; check for arbitration and for venue outside the accepted list.

Assignment/successors clause should be in the closing miscellaneous provisions before sec-p0072. Confirm we may assign to affiliates and successors and that HDI has no termination right on our change of control (relevant given HDI's affiliate relationship with Deerskin).

Direction rule. Key issue: ownership of the developed site, content, Deerskin Products imagery and customer/order data. sec-1.4 (HDI providing the Company access to systems and materials) and the development articles are the primary targets; flag only assignments of our IP or data to HDI.

sec-1.4 grants the Company access rights and is the closest thing to a licence grant. Test scope for affiliates and contractors and for revocability at will; note but do not flag purely stylistic gaps.

Parametric rule aimed at audits of the Company. Any inspection/records language would likely sit with the project-management and reporting provisions near sec-5.4; audits running in our favour against HDI are beneficial and must not be flagged.

Direction rule. Watch the fees/termination articles for penalties, early-termination charges or liquidated damages payable by the Company; credits or remedies running to us are welcome and not flagged.
Check the development/hosting services articles for an HDI performance or service-level warranty, its duration and remedy, plus any broad disclaimer of implied warranties that would gut it.

Missing-type rule. No insurance heading appears in the outline; HDI hosts the site and handles Company data, so if the body contains no insurance covenant, record as missing and propose standard coverages.
Presence rule. Look in the fees/compensation provisions for minimum spend, guaranteed volumes or take-or-pay hosting fees binding the Company; flag only if there is a commitment without an exit.

Missing-type rule tied to the 'Termination Date' machinery. Look for return of Company data, site content and access credentials (sec-1.4 access rights are the mirror image) plus migration assistance after termination; if absent, record as missing.
